AMZN.rationale: Amazon demonstrates strong fundamental health with accelerating revenue growth (Q1 2026: $181.5B, +16.6% YoY), record operating margins (13.1%), and AWS reaccelerating to 28% growth. The company's competitive position is dominant with 38-40% US e-commerce market share and 30% cloud market share. However, the $200B capex commitment for 2026 creates significant near-term free cash flow compression ($11.2B TTM FCF vs $38.2B prior year), and the stock has already rallied 33.9% in the past quarter, pushing the P/E to 37.9x—near the top of its 365-day range (28.2-39.0x). While the business trajectory is clearly positive with multiple growth engines (AWS, advertising, custom chips, logistics services), the valuation has moved from cheap (30x in March) to near-full, limiting upside. The upcoming Nvidia earnings (May 20) could serve as a sentiment catalyst for AI infrastructure names, but this is secondary to fundamentals. Net margin has improved to 11.1% from 10.1% a year ago, and ROE remains solid at 20.7%. The balance sheet is healthy with debt-to-equity of 0.149. Key risks include regulatory scrutiny (FTC lawsuit, California price-fixing case), tariff headwinds, and execution risk on the massive capex cycle.
key_factors: AWS reacceleration to 28% YoY growth—the fastest in 15 quarters—validates the AI infrastructure investment thesis
Record operating margin of 13.1% and net margin expansion to 11.1% demonstrate improving profitability across segments
$200B 2026 capex commitment compresses FCF to $11.2B but is backed by $244B AWS backlog and $225B Trainium chip commitments
P/E of 37.9x is near the top of its 365-day range (28.2-39.0x), having expanded from 30x in March—valuation is no longer cheap
Dominant competitive position: 38-40% US e-commerce share, 30% cloud share, advertising business now 4th largest globally at $70B+ TTM
Regulatory headwinds including FTC antitrust lawsuit and California price-fixing case create ongoing overhang
Stock has rallied 33.9% in the past quarter, suggesting much of the positive fundamental trajectory may be priced in

sources_cited.excerpt: Revenue came in at $181.52 billion, a 16.61% year-over-year improvement. GAAP earnings per share landed at $2.78. Net income reached $30.26 billion, up 76.65% year-over-year. Operating income of $23.9 billion produced an operating margin of 13.1%—the highest efficiency mark in Amazon's entire history.
AWS grew 28% year-over-year to $37.6 billion in revenue—the fastest pace in fifteen quarters—and threw off operating income of $14.2 billion, which represented a roughly 50% annual advance.

Amazon claimed the top spot among online retailers in the United States in 2025, capturing 40.5 percent of the market.
As of late 2025 Amazon holds an estimated 38.5 percent of the US e-commerce market, roughly six times Walmart's share.
